# wallix-bastion_timeframe (Data Source)

Get information on a timeframe resource, including its configured access periods and whether
sessions may run past the end of the timeframe.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get information about a specific timeframe
data "wallix-bastion_timeframe" "business_hours" {
  timeframe_name = "business_hours"
}

# Assign the looked-up timeframe to a user group
resource "wallix-bastion_usergroup" "day_shift" {
  group_name = "day_shift_operators"
  timeframes = [data.wallix-bastion_timeframe.business_hours.timeframe_name]
}

# Report whether sessions can overrun the timeframe
output "allows_overtime" {
  value = data.wallix-bastion_timeframe.business_hours.is_overtimable
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `timeframe_name` (String)

### Read-Only

- `description` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `is_overtimable` (Boolean)
- `periods` (Set of Object) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--periods))

<a id="nestedatt--periods"></a>

### Nested Schema for `periods`

Read-Only:

- `end_date` (String)
- `end_time` (String)
- `start_date` (String)
- `start_time` (String)
- `week_days` (Set of String)

## Usage Notes

### `timeframe_name`

The Required lookup key. It must match an existing timeframe exactly; the data source fails with
an error if no timeframe with that name exists.

### `periods`

A set of blocks, one per configured access period:

- **start_date/end_date**: Date range in `yyyy-mm-dd` format
- **start_time/end_time**: Time range in `hh:mm` format (24-hour), interpreted in the Bastion
  server's timezone
- **week_days**: The set of week days (`monday` through `sunday`) the period applies to

A timeframe can have multiple periods (e.g. split shifts, seasonal variations); since `periods` is
a set, do not rely on element order when consuming it.

### `is_overtimable`

Whether sessions already in progress are allowed to continue past the timeframe's end time
(`true`) or are terminated at the timeframe boundary (`false`).
